classification.difficultyReason: Translate Mary's second turn into the fourth roll, recognise that the game must survive the first three rolls, and multiply the three non-double probabilities and one double probability.

content.prompt: Bob and Mary take turns rolling a pair of dice. The first person to roll a double wins the game. Bob rolls first. Find the probability that Mary wins the game on her second turn.

answer.short:
$\frac{125}{1296}$

The first three rolls must be non-doubles, followed by a double.
answer.worked:
A double occurs on 6 of the 36 equally likely outcomes, so its probability is $\frac16$ and the probability of no double is $\frac56$. The first three turns are Bob, Mary, Bob. All three must fail to roll a double before Mary rolls one on the fourth turn.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Mary wins on her second turn})&=\left(\frac56\right)^3\times\frac16\\P(\text{Mary wins on her second turn})&=\frac{125}{1296}.\end{align*}$$
